articles.excerpt: Retro game retrospective #6 — 1992, Novotrade / Sega, Sega Genesis In 1992, the Sega Genesis was a machine of speed and aggression: hedgehogs, gunslingers, streets full of rage. Then Sega shipped a ga…
articles.body: Retro game retrospective #6 — 1992, Novotrade / Sega, Sega Genesis In 1992, the Sega Genesis was a machine of speed and aggression: hedgehogs, gunslingers, streets full of rage. Then Sega shipped a game where your hero can't punch, kick, or shoot — he can only swim, breathe, and sing . Ecco the Dolphin is a game about being a dolphin, built with a dolphin's senses, and it's one of the strangest, most technically inventive titles of the 16-bit era. This is the story of how a Hungarian studio turned echolocation into a game mechanic — and why developers should still be studying it. Novotrade / Sega, 1992 (Genesis). The North American box art: Ecco mid-leap, all muscle and mystery — promising an ocean, hiding an alien invasion.

articles.title: Detect breaking API changes in CI with OpenAPI diffs (before your customers do)
articles.excerpt: Every API team has a postmortem that starts with "we didn't think that was a breaking change." A field that was always present becomes optional; an enum gains a value clients treat as exhaustive; a re…
articles.body: Every API team has a postmortem that starts with "we didn't think that was a breaking change." A field that was always present becomes optional; an enum gains a value clients treat as exhaustive; a response code changes from 200 to 201; a query parameter that used to be ignored is now required. None of these show up in code review as dangerous, because code review shows the server diff, not the contract diff. The fix is boring and extremely effective: diff the OpenAPI document against the last released version in CI, classify changes automatically, and block the breaking ones. Here is how to set it up and what the classifier must understand. What actually counts as breaking Breaking means a change that can make a correctly written existing client fail.

articles.title: How a race condition stopped UK air traffic control for six hours
articles.excerpt: On Tuesday, September 8, 2026, UK air traffic control lost its core flight data link and stopped departures from British airfields for about four and a half hours. More than 2,000 flights were delayed…
articles.body: On Tuesday, September 8, 2026, UK air traffic control lost its core flight data link and stopped departures from British airfields for about four and a half hours. More than 2,000 flights were delayed, cancelled or diverted. The cause, according to the preliminary report by NATS , the UK's air traffic service, was a legacy software defect with an exposure window of about one millisecond. Programmers have a name for that kind of bug: a race condition. This is the postmortem, read the way a developer reads it. TL;DR At 10:00 a valid, correctly made request for a squawk code was paused part-way through updating a value, so a higher-priority message could be handled.

articles.body: 5 Min Read Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will head home from the International Space Station after supporting research that benefits life on Earth and prepares humans for missions into deep space. Here’s a look back at some of their accomplishments: Orbital transit NASA/ESA The crew members look out the window of a Dragon spacecraft during their journey to the space station, a destination that offers a unique vantage point to observe both Earth and the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA’s DAVINCI Probe Can Stand the Heat
articles.excerpt: The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI…
articles.body: An engineering model of NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) descent probe passed a key test that ran from Aug. 28 to Sept. 10, showing it can survive the extreme temperatures of Venus. NASA/Mike Guinto The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI team put the yoga ball-sized vessel into a ceramic-lined chamber with heat-scorched walls and ratcheted up the temperature to 869 F, or 465 C, over the course of about an hour — the same pace the probe will heat up during its descent to the surface of Venus.

articles.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
articles.excerpt: New helpful little guy just dropped. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge It's a tale as old as last week: OpenAI's new agent platform, called Dots, is full of cute little guys who can do your bidding…
articles.body: New helpful little guy just dropped. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge It's a tale as old as last week: OpenAI's new agent platform , called Dots, is full of cute little guys who can do your bidding. But unlike the ultra-approachable Meta Muse, Dots feel very much like using workplace software that happens to be able to order you a burrito - emphasis on work. OpenAI announced Dots earlier this week. Like Muse, Dots have blobby, anthropomorphic avatars and customizable names. In the future, OpenAI says you'll be able to have multiple Dots, but right now you get one. I named mine Dotty McDotface. articles.body: El equipo de control de vuelo de Artemis II, en la Sala Blanca de Control de Vuelo del centro de control de misiones del Centro Espacial Johnson de la NASA, en Houston, el 10 de abril de 2026, durante el amerizaje y la recuperación de la misión Artemis II. Crédito: NASA/Robert Markowitz Lee esta nota de prensa en inglés aquí . La NASA busca líderes para uno de los puestos más prestigiosos de la Tierra en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados: director de vuelo en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson de la agencia, en Houston. Esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo estadounidense en la exploración espacial, a medida que la NASA allana el camino hacia una presencia humana sostenida en la Luna.

articles.title: NASA Opens Applications for Next Class of Flight Directors
articles.excerpt: NASA is seeking leaders for one of the most esteemed positions on Earth for human spaceflight: flight director in mission control at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. This role is critical…
articles.body: The Artemis II flight control team is pictured in the White Flight Control Room in mission control at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on April 10, 2026, for the splashdown and recovery of the Artemis II mission. Credit: NASA/Robert Markowitz NASA is seeking leaders for one of the most esteemed positions on Earth for human spaceflight: flight director in mission control at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. This role is critical to advancing American leadership in space exploration, as NASA paves the way for a sustained human presence on the Moon. Applications for new flight directors are open now through Monday, Oct. 12. U.S.
